newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat propels oil complex to higher finish.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat propels oil complex to higher finish.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex ended with steep gains Wednesday propelled by a rally in heating oil ahead of weekly oil inventory data.
"It was the cold weather that was fueling this thing. They were focusing on today and not warmer weather forecasted soon," said a trader.
December heating oil settled up 2.95 cents at 71.20 cents a gallon.
Temperatures are expected to be about 11 to 15 degrees below normal in the U.S. Northeast throughout the week. The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis expects temperatures to moderate to normal to slightly above normal next week.
December crude ended up 77 cents at $24.12 a barrel.
"The products led crude today. Gasoline continued to rise on a strong cash market," said a trader.
December gasoline settled 2.57 cents higher at 68.34 cents a gallon.
After the market's close Wednesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported a draw of 827,000 barrels in distillate stocks, which includes heating oil, for the week ended November 8.
"The rally in heating oil was driven by two factors, cold temperatures here and abroad and the possibility of a draw in stocks," said Nauman Barakat, a trader with Prudential in New York.
Some traders had been expecting a slight build in distillates in the range of 500,000 to one million barrels.
Dealers said Wednesday's rally was also technically driven after buy stops in crude and heating oil were triggered when prices broke through resistance levels.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
